recommendation: Give an eligible executable opposite intent exit precedence whenever its symbol already has an open position.
why_now: The operator explicitly required opposite-signal profit capture, and an exact router reproduction showed that pre-position conflict ranking could suppress a valid opposite exit behind a stronger same-direction intent.
observed_problem_or_opportunity: With an open BTC long, an eligible short from one executable provider and a higher-ranked long from another produced no close. Provider conflict selection happened before position interaction.
applicable_market_regime: All regimes; this is deterministic open-position lifecycle semantics rather than a directional edge or regime filter.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Retain regime-and-priority ranking before position interaction
alternatives_considered.reason: It can suppress a valid opposite exit and contradicts the operator-approved lifecycle rule.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Close on every raw, stale, observe-only, or ineligible opposite hint
alternatives_considered.reason: Those rows lack execution authority and could manufacture exits from non-routable evidence.

alternatives_considered.alternative: Prioritize eligible executable opposite intents, then rank multiple valid exits normally
alternatives_considered.reason: It satisfies the requested exit rule while preserving provider authority, deterministic arbitration, and no same-cycle reversal.

proposed_live_change: When a symbol is open, choose from eligible enter_and_close intents opposite the venue position before considering same-direction intents. If several valid opposite exits exist, retain existing regime, provider-priority, and decision-time ordering.
expected_upside: Avoid preventable profit giveback or stop loss when an executable opposite signal exists but a competing same-direction provider would otherwise suppress it.
main_risks_and_failure_modes: An economically weak but executable opposite provider can close a stronger incumbent lifecycle; this is the explicitly requested lifecycle rule and must remain attributable.
A raw or observe-only hint must not be admitted as an exit.
The close must not reverse or open the opposite position in the same cycle.
The running backend predates this source revision and must not be described as containing the change before a verified restart.

validation_completed.tdd_red: The new exact conflict regression failed with zero actions before the fix.
validation_completed.tdd_green: The same regression passed after position-aware exit precedence was implemented.
validation_completed.focused_and_broader_tests: 79 routing/runner/telemetry tests passed; 22 exact v51/router tests passed, including the profile-bound HYPE close-only falsifier.
validation_completed.static_checks: Ruff check passed, Ruff format check passed, and git diff --check passed.

validation_still_required: Reach a verified flat and owned-order-free boundary before any restart.
Create and verify the mandatory prestart implementation backup for the successor process.
After restart, prove the active implementation identity includes this source hash.
Observe an attributable live conflict or controlled non-order integration replay showing an eligible opposite closes and same-cycle reversal remains suppressed.
success_metrics: Every open-symbol cycle containing at least one eligible executable opposite intent emits exactly one close action.
No same-cycle opposite entry is emitted after that close.
Same-direction-only cycles remain holds/withheld rather than closes.
Observe-only, stale, ineligible, and flat-entry-only intents cannot close a position.
failure_or_rollback_triggers: An eligible executable opposite is recorded without a close action.
A non-executable or stale opposite closes a position.
A close and reverse entry occur in one cycle.
Restart identity or venue/ledger reconciliation fails.
confidence_basis: The defect was reproduced and the source behavior is covered across router, live-runner, audit, authority-isolation, regime-conflict, and exact-v51 tests. No post-restart live conflict has occurred yet.
falsifier: Any authoritative post-restart cycle in which a valid executable opposite is admitted for an open symbol but no close is routed, or any cycle in which an unauthorized opposite causes a close.
